chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)far (peace be upon him) who said:

When you stand in the prayer, do not join your foot with the other; leave a gap between them of a finger's width, the least of that being up to a span, and more is allowed. Drop your shoulders, extend your hands, do not interlace your fingers, and let them rest on your thighs in front of your knees, and let your gaze be towards the place of your prostration.

When you bow, align your feet in your bowing, placing between them a span's distance. Place your palms upon your knees, placing your right hand on your right knee before the left. Reach the tips of your fingers to the center of the knee, and spread your fingers when you place them on your knees. When the tips of your fingers reach your knees during bowing, that suffices you. And what I love is that you place your palms firmly on your knees, so your fingers are in the center of the knee and you spread between them. Straighten your back, extend your neck, and let your gaze be towards what is between your feet.

When you intend to prostrate, raise your hands with the Takbir and fall down prostrating. Begin with your hands, placing them on the ground before your knees, placing them together. Do not spread your forearms flat like a beast spreads its forearms, nor place your forearms on your knees and thighs. Rather, wing with your elbows. Do not join your palms to your knees, nor bring them close to your face; they should be parallel to your shoulders. Do not place them directly in front of your knees, but divert them slightly from that. Extend them on the ground with an extension, and pull them towards you with a pull.

And if there is a garment beneath them, it does not harm you. And if you lead them to the ground, that is better. And do not spread between your fingers during your prostration, but gather them all together.

He said: And when you sit for your Tashahhud, join your knees to the ground and separate between them slightly. Let the back of your left foot be on the ground, and the back of your right foot be on the inside of your left foot. Let your buttocks be on the ground, and the tip of your right big toe be on the ground. Beware of sitting on your two feet, for you will be hurt by that. And do not sit on the ground such that part of you is on part of the other, so that you cannot endure the Tashahhud and the supplication.
ai.seo_question: What are the detailed physical postures and etiquette for standing, bowing, and prostrating in Shia Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) codifies the 'Sunnah of the Prophet' regarding physical precision in prayer, distinguishing Shia jurisprudence through specific details like spreading fingers in Ruku and the exact placement of hands in Sujood. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on 'Adab al-Salat' (etiquette of prayer) as a means to enhance Khushu (concentration), linking bodily discipline to spiritual presence.
